classification.difficultyReason: Apply the cross-section rule while the container empties: descending water encounters smaller areas, so depth decreases increasingly quickly and the negative gradient becomes steeper.

content.prompt:
The container shown is initially full of water.

Water leaks out of the bottom of the container at a constant rate.

Which graph best shows the depth of water in the container as time varies?

spec.description: Open inverted conical container with a broad elliptical water surface and a small bottom outlet. Light blue surface fill replaces source stippling.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal cross-section becomes smaller towards the bottom; no numerical dimensions are supplied.

spec.description: Option A: straight decreasing depth–time graph; arrowed axes extend left and below their intersection. Source origin O is omitted under house convention.
spec.mathematics: Depth decreases at a constant rate to zero; axes have no numerical scale.

spec.description: Option B: horizontal positive-depth graph; arrowed axes extend left and below their intersection. Source origin O is omitted under house convention.
spec.mathematics: Depth remains constant; axes have no numerical scale.

spec.description: Option C: decreasing curve initially steep and progressively flattening to zero. Source origin O is omitted under house convention.
spec.mathematics: Depth decreases at a decreasing rate; axes have no numerical scale and the curve is qualitative.

spec.description: Option D: decreasing curve initially shallow and becoming progressively steeper, ending almost vertically at zero. Source origin O is omitted under house convention.
spec.mathematics: Depth decreases at an increasing rate; axes have no numerical scale and the curve is qualitative.

answer.worked: As the water level falls, the container's cross-section becomes smaller. With water leaking out at a constant rate, the depth therefore decreases faster, so the graph becomes progressively steeper downwards. Correct answer: D.
